title: Rollout Convergence Inspector & Shadow Telemetry
creator: Lina Park
description: Build a Console feature called 'Convergence Inspector' that gives engineers a compact, time-aware view for comparing cohorts during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts. The feature should surface per-route metric deltas (latency p50/p90/p99, token cost, error-rate), a divergence score over time, and linked traces/playback for outlier requests. Shadow traffic telemetry will be integrated to show continuous divergence even when traffic is mirrored, and automatic rollback suggestion signals will be emitted when sustained divergence exceeds thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: A: Console shows side-by-side cohort overview for any two cohorts with selectable time windows
B: Per-route deltas include latency p50/p90/p99, token usage delta, success/error rate, and throughput change
C: Divergence score computed and plotted as time series; hover reveals contributing metrics
D: Trace links are available from the Inspector to the Trace Viewer for top-N anomalous requests
E: Shadow telemetry panel shows mirrored traffic divergence and a summary signal that can be used by auto-rollback rules
F: Product tests validate that the auto-rollback suggestion triggers when configured thresholds are exceeded for >= 5 mins
G: UX and copy reviewed and approved by Design and PM; Figma prototype linked
engineering_notes: Backend: new rollout-inspector API that queries per-route time-bucketed stats from telemetry store (rollup by 1m/5m) and computes divergence score

Divergence score: weighted aggregate of z-scored p99 latency, error rate uplift, and token-cost drift. Prototype uses Holt-Winters for baseline smoothing; plan to benchmark against quantile-diff approach
Trace linking: include sample request IDs and route->trace_id mapping emitted by the runtime. ENG-23145 will add sample headers in shadow requests
Performance: inspector queries limited to 3 routes per view initially to prevent heavy aggregation joins; will iterate after benching
Security: ensure trace links honor project RBAC and PII redaction policies
test_plan: Unit tests for divergence score computation (edge cases: low-volume routes, zero-traffic cohorts)
Integration test: end-to-end rollouts using synthetic traffic generator to produce controlled divergence patterns
E2E: QA run with internal canary to validate UX and trace linking before beta release
Load: backend aggregator tested with synthetic 10k reqs/min across 50 routes to validate 30s UI load target
rollout_impact: Will enable platform engineers to detect silent regressions earlier during canary and A/B tests
Auto-rollback suggestion reduces time-to-mitigation for high-impact regressions (estimated 40% reduction in mean time to rollback during pilot)
Initial release limited to hosted customers and Redwood Dedicated tenants with telemetry enabled
decisions: Show p50/p90/p99 by default; users can expand to custom percentiles
Divergence score will be visible as ordinal (low/medium/high) and a continuous metric to power automation rules
Shadow telemetry will sample 1% of mirrored traces by default to control storage costs (configurable per workspace)
Auto-rollback suggestion only surfaces (not automatic action) in v1; later iteration will add opt-in automatic rollback
milestones: 2026-03-07: Backend API schema & divergence algorithm prototype complete
2026-03-14: Frontend prototype (Figma -> React prototype) and basic integration with trace links
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Divergence score false positives on very low traffic routes -> Mitigation: apply minimum traffic threshold and confidence intervals
Risk: Storage and cost growth from trace capture -> Mitigation: sample rate default 1%, allow workspace overrides, and compress traces for mirror traffic
Risk: Users misinterpret suggestion as auto-rollback -> Mitigation: clear UI copy and require an explicit enable flag for automation
